about: The engine keeps launch and listen; carrying a call between computers is a tool (the person's ruling of Nov 15 2026: anything that is not one of the five core jobs is a tool and leaves the engine). The forwarder (src/forwarder and src/forwarder.rs: the public door's route table, the Mac-initiated session, the connected computers, origins, the gateway), the engine's outbound HTTPS client (src/https.rs and src/https/), the signed authority a forwarder connection is admitted by (src/signed_authority.rs), the forwarder binary (src/bin) and the Mac side's two carriers (src/native_boot/forwarder_connection.rs and mcp_outbound.rs) move into one Workshop tool folder, at the same paths under src/ so their include_bytes!, include_str! and #[path] reads still reach their neighbours. Rust files are not followed for imports; the group names every file. This tree is public and holds made-up data only: three call rows swap what a public push refuses (a real first name in one README sentence, an example email shape in two tests, and one literal certificate header in a test string, written as the same bytes with an escape); every other byte is the source's.

calls.means: A real person's first name, matched by its place (the sentence that names the date and the sign-in decision), becomes a made-up role word.
A URL with user information on a made-up .test host reads as a real email address to the public push check; the same test on the example.com host keeps its meaning (user information is refused).
The test's header literal is written with its first dash as a byte escape, so the string holds the same bytes at run time and the source holds no whole certificate header.

groups.capability: carry a call between computers: the public door's route table, a Mac's confidential session to it, the connected computers it routes to, and the one HTTPS client the engine's outbound calls use
